report.summary: Reviewed bus.py chunk 3 of 3 (public append API, reading, verify_chain); enumerated claims and observations.
risks: append_round | medium | Duplicate detection excludes 'council.redacted.redacted' only for the duplicate check, but a duplicate anonymized receipt for a different actor could still be chained; the sort tiebreak may not be sufficient to guarantee exactly-one-per-actor if two different actors collapse to the same redacted actor. | Would settle: trace _refusal_receipt and the sort key to see if two distinct actors can produce identical (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json) tuples and still be chained as separate turns.

verify_chain | medium | The per-line check for entry_sha uses rec.get('ts', '') but _entry_sha may expect a specific ts format; if the ts is missing or malformed, the check may produce a mismatch that is actually a format issue rather than tampering. | Would settle: inspect _entry_sha to see how it handles missing/empty ts and whether the stored ts is always present in valid records.

verify_chain | medium | The docstring claims 'every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line' but the tail/head/record-count failures do not name a line (they name the whole file). | Would settle: confirm whether the claim is meant to apply only to per-line checks.

append_roster | medium | The 'degraded' flag is set to True when a rule is triggered, but the docstring does not state that; the refusal path may be unreachable if _scan_roster never returns a rule for a roster with valid inputs. | Would settle: inspect _scan_roster to see if it can ever return a rule for a roster that passed the validation above.

load_transcript | low | The docstring says 'skipping a torn tail line' but the implementation skips any unparseable line, not just the tail; a corrupt line in the middle is silently dropped, which could hide tampering. | Would settle: confirm whether the intent is to skip only the last line or any line; the docstring's 'torn tail line' suggests only the last line.

handoff.purpose: Public append API, transcript reading, and tamper verification functions.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Chains a whole round; normalizes, secret-floors, sorts by actor/role/status/canonical body, and chains with seq assigned here. Rejects empty turns and duplicate non-redacted actors. Refuses turns that trigger a rule, replacing with a refusal receipt (anonymous fallback). Returns ids in chained order.

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper for append_round with a single turn; returns the single id.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Chains a roster accounting record. Validates phase, participant keys, actor format, and outcome. Computes counts (requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, duplicate_classes) and degraded flag. If a rule is triggered, replaces participants with [] and sets refused. Returns the chained record's id.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Reads all records from a transcript file, skipping blank lines and lines that fail to parse as JSON. Missing file returns [].

symbols.name: transcript_head
symbols.note: Returns (record_count, head_entry_sha) by loading the transcript and reading the last record's entry_sha (or None if empty).

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads the anchor file and returns its JSON dict, or None if the file is missing or unparseable.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Walks the transcript and verifies body_sha, entry_sha, and prev linkage per line. Optionally consults the anchor for expected count/head. Returns (ok, failures) with named failures.

claims.text: turns may arrive in ANY completion order
claims.why: Turns are sorted by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json) before chaining, so completion order does not affect the chain.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with seq assigned here
claims.why: Each turn goes through _normalize_turn (which presumably includes secret flooring), then prepared.sort uses actor as the primary sort key, and _chain_records assigns seq.

claims.text: reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head
claims.why: The sort key is deterministic and independent of input order, so the same set of turns produces the same chained sequence regardless of the order they arrive in.

claims.text: Returns the ids in CHAINED order
claims.why: _chain_records returns ids in the order the records were chained, which is the sorted order.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice
claims.why: The code detects duplicates among actors (excluding 'council.redacted.redacted') and raises ValueError.

claims.text: a missing participant must be recorded as an unavailable turn rather than skipped
claims.why: The docstring states a policy for missing participants, but this chunk does not show how unavailable turns are handled (it only shows the duplicate check and the refusal path).

claims.text: The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, and not in the receipt.
claims.why: The comment claims that refused turns are replaced with a receipt that does not contain the offending bytes. This chunk does not show the implementation of _refusal_receipt, so we cannot verify that the receipt is free of the offending bytes.

claims.text: Canonical body is the final tiebreak so the order is TOTAL even when two anonymised refusal receipts collapse to the same actor
claims.why: The sort key includes canonical_body_json(r), which would break ties if two receipts have the same actor, role, and status but different canonical bodies. However, we cannot verify that canonical_body_json is always distinct for two distinct receipts, nor that the sort is total without inspecting that function.

claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round)
claims.why: append_turn calls append_round with a single-turn list, which chains exactly one record.

claims.text: Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: append_turn delegates to append_round; the docstring's advice is consistent with the implementation.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons
claims.why: The record includes 'requested', 'seated', 'responded', 'unavailable' fields, and each participant has a 'reason' field.

claims.text: plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count
claims.why: The record includes 'distinct_classes' computed as len(set(heard_classes)).

claims.text: a degraded flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested
claims.why: The record includes 'degraded' set to responded < requested.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller
claims.why: All counts (requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, duplicate_classes, degraded) are computed from the normalized participant list, not taken from caller input.

claims.text: 3 of 4 and 2 of 2 must not be able to render as the same string
claims.why: The counts are stored as separate integer fields, so they cannot collapse into the same string unless a consumer chooses to render them that way.

claims.text: a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council
claims.why: The record provides both 'requested' and 'distinct_classes'; the docstring warns against using the wrong one, and the code ensures the distinct-class count is available.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: The implementation skips ANY line that fails to parse as JSON, not just the tail. A torn line in the middle would also be silently skipped, contradicting the 'torn tail line' wording. (Line 641: except json.JSONDecodeError: continue)

claims.text: (record_count, head_entry_sha) -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file
claims.why: transcript_head loads the transcript and returns len(records) and the last record's entry_sha, which is the head entry sha.

claims.text: Compare against :func:`read_anchor` to catch a truncation.
claims.why: The function returns the head sha and count, which can be compared to the anchor's count and head.

claims.text: Walk the chain; return (ok, failures) where every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line and what mismatched. Never a bare False.
claims.why: All per-line failures include 'line {i}'; the final count/head failures name the file rather than a line, but they are not per-line failures. The function returns a tuple, never a bare False.

claims.text: body_sha recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit
claims.why: The code compares _body_sha(rec) to stored_body.

claims.text: entry_sha recomputed over (prev, stored body_sha, ts) -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated
claims.why: The code compares _entry_sha(rec.get('prev'), stored_body or '', rec.get('ts', '')) to stored_entry.

claims.text: prev equals the previous line's entry_sha -- catches a deleted or reordered line
claims.why: The code compares rec.get('prev') to prev_entry_sha and updates prev_entry_sha to stored_entry after each record.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch (a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain), so the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED.
claims.why: When use_anchor is True and no explicit expectations are given, the anchor is read and expected_count/expected_head are set; later shortfalls are reported.

claims.text: Explicit expected_count / expected_head override it; use_anchor=False verifies linkage only.
claims.why: The code only consults the anchor when use_anchor is True and both expected_count and expected_head are None.

observations.what: load_transcript skips any unparseable line, not just the tail, contradicting the docstring's 'torn tail line' wording.
verify_chain's per-line failure messages name the line, but the count/head failures do not name a line; the docstring's 'every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line' is slightly overstated.

append_round's duplicate check excludes 'council.redacted.redacted' only; if two different actors both produce redacted receipts with identical sort keys, the duplicate check would not catch them, and the chain would contain two turns for the same redacted actor.
append_roster's refusal path sets 'degraded' to True unconditionally, even if responded >= requested before the rule; the docstring does not mention this behavior.
verify_chain uses rec.get('ts', '') when recomputing entry_sha; if a record lacks a ts field, the recomputation uses an empty string, which may or may not match the original computation.
